Review an OAuth client configuration before deployment

Source: R/check_oauth21.R
check_oauth21.Rd

Check a configured OAuthClient for missing settings and recommendations. The result includes a table of findings and suggested fixes. The check is read-only: it does not make requests, start login or change the configuration.

Usage

check_oauth21(config, context = list(), draft = "draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-16")

Arguments

config

An OAuthClient or OAuthProvider. A provider-only report is partial because it cannot check your client registration settings.

context

Optional list. operations selects additional "userinfo", "introspection" or "revocation" checks. The advanced nonce_exception declaration is described below; most apps should leave it unset.

draft

Target specification revision. Currently only "draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-16" is supported; this is an Internet-Draft, not an RFC.

Value

A shinyOAuth_oauth21_assessment list. checks is a data frame with id, scope, status, requirement, message, remediation, reference, evidence_source, requirement_source and affects_verdict columns. Statuses are pass, fail, warn, unknown and not_applicable. Only rows with affects_verdict = TRUE affect configuration_compliant. A compatibility warn does not by itself fail the verdict. The report also records draft, ruleset_version, package_version, assessed_at, assessment_scope and operations.

Details

Call assessment <- check_oauth21(client), then read assessment$checks. assessment$configuration_compliant is FALSE for a known mandatory failure, NA for unresolved mandatory settings, and TRUE when the applicable mandatory configuration checks pass. Recommendations and unknown external behavior do not change that result.

This assessment uses OAuth 2.1 draft 16, ruleset 1.1.1. It is not certification or a test of your running provider. Rerun it after changing configuration.

Advanced assessment scope

Checks cover code exchange, refresh, enabled PAR, required UserInfo and introspection, selected extra operations and applicable signing-key retrieval. Optional DPoP, mTLS, PAR, JAR and JARM are not required together. Provider enforcement, registered redirects, secret storage, browser/proxy TLS and future API requests need separate deployment checks.

mTLS file paths do not establish that a certificate and key are readable and match. The checker does not open them, so applicable mtls.credentials.* checks remain unknown when paths are present; missing required paths fail. Actual requests validate the current files.

requirement_source distinguishes protocol requirements from security guidance and package policy. Callback capacity thresholds are package recommendations, not numeric limits from the draft. Reports exclude credentials, keys, endpoint URLs and the configuration objects. Cache and state-store methods are not run.

Advanced PKCE exception

context = list(nonce_exception = TRUE) declares independently established server assurance for the draft's confidential-client nonce exception (section 7.5.1.1). It does not supply observed evidence or bypass missing local requirements. Prefer S256 PKCE. Assertion audience checks are mandatory for JWT authentication; advice about the legacy JWT assertion type is a recommendation.

References

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-16

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-rfc7523bis-11

https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9207.html

Examples

provider <- oauth_provider(
  name = "Example",
  auth_url = "https://auth.example/authorize",
  token_url = "https://auth.example/token",
  token_auth_style = "public", use_pkce = TRUE, pkce_method = "S256"
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider, client_id = "example-client",
  redirect_uri = "https://app.example/callback"
)
assessment <- check_oauth21(client)
assessment[["checks"]][assessment[["checks"]][["status"]] != "pass", ]
